Brevig–Søvik arXiv:2610.21788, coefficient-functional outer polynomial corollary
correctness.rationale: For every fixed k>=1 and p downarrow 0, the cited outer-polynomial extremizer representation reduces the sharp H^p Taylor coefficient functional to the degree-k unit H2 coefficient sphere. Generalized binomial coefficients are positive for s=2/p>k, so replacing polynomial coefficients by absolute values gives a valid upper bound; the eventual optimal polynomial is zero-free and hence admissible. The exponential tail bound confines rescaled u_j=sqrt(s)a_j, and the limit exp(-||u||^2/2)u_1^k/k! has the unique maximizer (sqrt(k),0,..), strictly negative Hessian (-2c,-c,...). Analytic implicit-function perturbation yields u_2=(k-1)/sqrt(s)+O(1/s), the correction ((k-1)^2+1)/(4s), eventual phase/rotation uniqueness, and P_s(w/sqrt(s))^s -> exp(-k/2+sqrt(k)w) compactly. Independent symbolic consistency verified the direct second-order term -k^2/4+k/2 and u2 optimization (k-1)^2/2 against the predicted coefficient for k=1..4; these finite checks are not proof of all k.
residual_risks: The only nonstandard external premise is the Brevig–Søvik outer polynomial extremizer reduction; the infinite analytic proof is not established by the finite check alone.
